text:
QUOTE: "The text before the first `:` is an fnmatch glob on the fully-qualified tool name, e.g. `filesystem.*`. - With no `:`, the tool-name match is enough. A bare `bash.execute` allows every call to that tool. - With a `:`, the part after it is an fnmatch glob on the argument pattern"
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states fnmatch matching, the split at the first colon into tool and argument parts, and that a colon-less pattern matches on tool name alone.
